topic.title: From 0.684 toward top 1%: what validation evidence predicts real gains?
topic.author: Pengyi Peng1

raw.title: From 0.684 toward top 1%: what validation evidence predicts real gains?
From 0.684 toward top 1%: what validation evidence predicts real gains?

firstMessage.content:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to improve a reproducible baseline toward the top 1% while avoiding leaderboard overfitting. I would appreciate feedback on validation and model complementarity rather than private weights or test-label heuristics.

Current evidence, as of 12 November: my best public score is 0.684, an attributed reproduction of Areeb Ali's v11, not my original ensemble. My snapshot is 308/5575 teams; strict top 1% is rank 55, whose displayed score is 0.705. Rank 56 is also 0.705, so a tied score is not a guarantee. Public standings are provisional,not final medals.

What did not establish a gain: three small row-local residuals moved a separate CPU component's prompt-grouped macro recall from 0.385185 to at best 0.391204. Corrected paired intervals crossed zero and sparse-prompt diagnostics regressed. These are reused development results,not fresh holdout evidence, and are not comparable with the full ensemble's 0.684 public score. One exploratory variant is still being scored;its result is unknown.

I published a small CPU Validation Lab: original standard-library helpers for 18-class macro recall, prompt-overlap rejection and deterministic paired prompt-cluster intervals. Its executed examples are synthetic only; it is not a top 1% inference model or new submission.

My proposed next experiment is ONE complementary representation/family specialist, with matched prompt-disjoint OOF for the complete incumbent, calibration fitted inside folds, external-source/duplicate audits and per-class plus one/two/many-row prompt checks. Full-ensemble OOF is still missing,not a completed validation claim. I found the earlier grouped-CV and transfer discussion helpful, particularly its warning that group-based local gains may not transfer.

Questions:

  1. Which prompt-held-out and external-source-held-out protocol has best predicted transfer for you? How do you audit same-prompt regeneration and duplicates in external data without querying/tuning on the public leaderboard?
  2. With balanced accuracy and changing model priors, which fold-safe calibration, per-class recall or family-confusion diagnostics identify genuinely complementary embedding/LoRA models? Public,license-compatible ablations would be helpful.
  3. How do you verify that the tested post-processing actually executes in the full hidden rerun, including tail batches, rather than only the tiny preview?

I will preserve negative findings and credit shared methods. Thanks for any specific methodological feedback or links to reproducible public work.

Pengyi Peng
